summary: The RNG offset reported at drown's water_damage_chain is downstream of an omitted dropx call in emergency_disrobe. C selects a droppable inventory object, calls dropx, and then decrements invc; JS records note_unported('do.c dropx') and decrements invc without removing or landing the object. The retained inventory changes later water_damage_chain contents and the RNG stream. Repair the existing emergency_disrobe caller to invoke the already implemented dropx/flooreffects/water_damage path.

source.branch: During drown's crawl-out attempt, when near_capacity exceeds the allowed load and emergency_disrobe selects a droppable inventory item, drop the selected object before decrementing the local inventory count.

evidence: Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/trap.c:4897-4944 selects otmp and calls dropx(otmp) before invc--; the only production caller is drown at trap.c:5157.

JS js/trap.js:1363-1404 mirrors the selection loop but replaces dropx with note_unported('do.c dropx'), leaving the selected object in inventory and on its original object chain while decrementing invc.

Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/do.c:782-797 removes the object from inventory and calls flooreffects; do.c:272-287 routes a pool landing through water_damage(obj, NULL, FALSE). Existing JS js/do.js:2113-2137 invokes the same drop tail, js/do.js:1000-1008 routes pool landings through water_damage, and js/trap_water_damage.js:568-659 implements that path.

Single-case diagnostic /tmp/teleport-validation-1000/run-fiSZC8/stdout.log (replay commit 9dda334742ff4b02ce9496bf2ff226d7227f1b2e) reproduces the saved step-138 mismatch and reports the active JS gap do.c dropx; the admitted queue attributes C's first unmatched draw to water_damage(trap.c:4771).

Prep16 source intake .cache/prep16-source-intake-reviewed.json independently identifies this case's earlier emergency_disrobe -> dropx omission and notes that the later water_damage RNG offset can follow from inventory that should already have been dropped.
